Title: The Royal Statutes of Barrowmark
Second Edition Author: ???

[The beginning of this book is pages upon pages describing the titles of the king (name pending), his domains, and then a lengthy talk about the saints and justice.]

Title First, of Duels

Let it be known that disputes of honor or grave matters may be tried by duel.

1.1 The noble may refuse challenges of the lowborn.
1.2 Duels shall be fought before witnesses on ground appointed by the lord.
1.3 Either party may fight by champion.
1.4 No hidden sorcery, poison, nor device shall be brought into combat.
1.5 Once a combatant yields or becomes unable to continue fighting, the victor shall be held as proven and his word true under the eyes of the saints.
1.6 To slay one who surrenders is murder, unless the duel was sworn to the death.
1.7 Refusal of a lawful duel brings loss of cause.

Title Second, of Infamy

All subjects shall speak the truth, keep faith, and abide by the law, lest they fall outside the protection of the fair lord.

1.1 Those who lie, break oath, or deceive lose their bond of trust and may be held infamous.
1.2 The lord may decree someone so infamous as to be denied the protection of the lord's courts, and barred from service and trade with all upstanding merchants.
1.3 Outlawing an individual may be done openly by the lord or sworn officers so that all may know.
1.4 Knowingly harboring or assisting outlaws may incur suspicion or penalties.
1.5 Repentance and restitution may restore standing, according to the judgment of the lord.

Title Third, of Killing

There shall be three kinds of killing: by accident, in self-defense, and in murder without cause.

1.1 Those who take a life by accident shall be free of guilt, provided they have taken all precautions to prevent such fate.
1.2 Self-defense is no crime if not the first blow, whether in one’s house, in battle, or against assailants.
1.3 Murder done without cause, in malice or envy, shall be punished as the lord or their sworn officer decrees.
1.4 Those who kill by command of the Lord are blameless.

Title Fourth, of Theft

None shall take what is not theirs.

1.1 Whoever takes coin, goods, or chattels without leave is a thief.
1.2 Those who aid or harbor a thief shall be judged accomplices.
1.3 Theft committed by force, stealth, or deception shall be judged accordingly.
1.4 That which is seized by the lord or agents thereof shall not be considered theft.

Title Fifth, of Sorcery and Heresy

Magic is a power most perilous, and shall be wielded only in service of God and the saints.

1.1 No perilous or unlawful sorcery shall be wrought within any town, village, or hold of the march.
1.2 Unlawful sorcery is any magic that goes against the saints.
1.3 None shall blaspheme against God or the saints, deny their miracles, or scorn the holy sacraments, lest they be judged heretic.
1.4 It is the right of the church to involve itself in judgement of heretics.

Title Sixth, of Punishment

These are the punishments the fair lord suggests to be used for those who transgress the laws of the realm, according to the severity of their offense.

1.1 For minor offenses: A warning, restitution of goods or coin, or service to the lord may suffice.
1.2 For offenses: Fines, public shaming, or corporal punishment may be imposed.
1.3 For great or violent offenses: Imprisonment, corporal punishment, exile, death, or outlawry may be applied.
1.4 Heresy: The church shall judge the heretic, and the lord may impose additional punishment should circumstances require it.
